panels.title: Monitoring Feed
panels.description: How long ago the last traffic record arrived. If this is not LIVE, every other panel on this screen is stale and nothing here can be trusted — escalate.

targets.query:
import "array"

// Seconds since the newest flow record. The sentinel means a dead feed shows
// NO DATA rather than an empty tile, which would look the same as "quiet".
latest = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: -6h, stop: now())
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> group()
  |> max(column: "_time")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({age: float(v: int(v: now()) - int(v: r._time)) / 1000000000.0}))
  |> keep(columns: ["age"])

union(tables: [latest, array.from(rows: [{age: 99999.0}])])
  |> group()
  |> min(column: "age")
  |> rename(columns: {age: "_value"})

panels.title: Traffic Now
panels.description: Current throughput across the mirror, with the recent trend behind it. Shown without a colour threshold on purpose: there is no fixed link capacity to alarm against, so judge it against the 'vs Yesterday' tile.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 5m, fn: sum, createEmpty: false)
  |> group()
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 5m, fn: sum, createEmpty: false)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, _value: float(v: r._value) * 8.0 / 300.0}))

panels.title: vs Yesterday
panels.description: Traffic in the last hour compared with the same hour yesterday. Measured on this network the ratio has a median of 98% and stays between 94% and 196% -- the upper end is the normal morning ramp, which is why NORMAL runs all the way to 250%: a band that went amber every morning would just be ignored. A collapse can mean an outage upstream, not merely a quiet network. Widen these bands if your traffic is burstier.

targets.query:
import "array"

win = (start, stop, tag) => from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: start, stop: stop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> group()
  |> sum()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({k: "x", w: tag, v: float(v: r._value)}))

// Zero rows for both sides so the pivot always has both columns, even if one
// window is empty.
zero = array.from(rows: [{k: "x", w: "now", v: 0.0}, {k: "x", w: "yest", v: 0.0}])

union(tables: [
  win(start: -1h, stop: now(), tag: "now"),
  win(start: -25h, stop: -24h, tag: "yest"),
  zero,
])
  |> group(columns: ["k", "w"])
  |> sum(column: "v")
  |> group()
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["k"], columnKey: ["w"], valueColumn: "v")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _value:
      if r.yest > 0.0 then r.now / r.yest * 100.0 else -1.0}))
  |> keep(columns: ["_value"])

panels.title: Active Hosts
panels.description: Distinct hosts seen sending traffic in the last 15 minutes. Context rather than an alarm — a sudden collapse usually shows up in 'vs Yesterday' first.

targets.query:
import "array"

// first() per series is a pushdown selector: one row per distinct source.
seen = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: -15m, stop: now())
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip"])
  |> first()
  |> group()
  |> count(column: "_value")
  |> keep(columns: ["_value"])

union(tables: [seen, array.from(rows: [{_value: 0}])])
  |> group()
  |> max()

panels.title: Peak Fan-Out
panels.description: The most destinations any single host contacted in the last 15 minutes. Two infrastructure hosts here normally sit in the 60-83 range, so NORMAL runs to 120 to leave them headroom. A host suddenly reaching hundreds of destinations is scanning.

targets.query:
import "array"

// Highest number of distinct destinations reached by any one host in 15
// minutes. Shown as a number rather than an alert count, because two
// infrastructure hosts here legitimately sit in the 60-80 range.
peak = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: -15m, stop: now())
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip", "dst_ip"])
  |> first()
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip"])
  |> count()
  |> group()
  |> max()
  |> keep(columns: ["_value"])

union(tables: [peak, array.from(rows: [{_value: 0}])])
  |> group()
  |> max()

panels.title: Busiest Host Share
panels.description: Share of all traffic generated by the single busiest host in the last 15 minutes. One host taking most of the link is normal during a big transfer, but sustained dominance is worth naming when you escalate.

targets.query:
import "array"

per = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: -15m, stop: now())
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip"])
  |> sum()

top = per |> group() |> max() |> map(fn: (r) => ({k: "x", w: "top", v: float(v: r._value)}))
tot = per |> group() |> sum() |> map(fn: (r) => ({k: "x", w: "tot", v: float(v: r._value)}))
zero = array.from(rows: [{k: "x", w: "top", v: 0.0}, {k: "x", w: "tot", v: 0.0}])

union(tables: [top, tot, zero])
  |> group(columns: ["k", "w"])
  |> sum(column: "v")
  |> group()
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["k"], columnKey: ["w"], valueColumn: "v")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _value:
      if r.tot > 0.0 then r.top / r.tot * 100.0 else 0.0}))
  |> keep(columns: ["_value"])

panels.title: Traffic — now vs same time yesterday
panels.description: Today's throughput over the selected window, with yesterday's same hours behind it for reference. If the two lines track each other, the network is behaving normally. A sustained gap is the thing to report.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 5m, fn: sum, createEmpty: false)
  |> group()
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 5m, fn: sum, createEmpty: false)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, _value: float(v: r._value) * 8.0 / 300.0, series: "Now"}))
  |> group(columns: ["series"])

import "date"

from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: date.sub(from: v.timeRangeStart, d: 24h), stop: date.sub(from: v.timeRangeStop, d: 24h))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 5m, fn: sum, createEmpty: false)
  |> group()
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 5m, fn: sum, createEmpty: false)
  |> timeShift(duration: 24h)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, _value: float(v: r._value) * 8.0 / 300.0, series: "Same time yesterday"}))
  |> group(columns: ["series"])

panels.title: Busiest Hosts
panels.description: The hosts moving the most data right now, with their names resolved so you can say who it is rather than reading out an IP address. Country is from a local GeoIP database (IP geolocation by DB-IP, db-ip.com); "private network" for any non-public address.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 8)
  |> rename(columns: {src_ip: "ip", _value: "bytes"})
  |> keep(columns: ["ip", "bytes"])

panels.title: What's running on the network
panels.description: Traffic grouped by what kind of application it is. Useful for answering "what is all this?" without reading a single port number.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> group(columns: ["category"])
  |> sum()
  |> keep(columns: ["category", "_value"])

panels.title: Busiest conversations
panels.description: The single heaviest source-to-destination pairs. This is the line to quote when escalating: who is talking to whom, and how much.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip", "dst_ip"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 8)
  |> keep(columns: ["src_ip", "dst_ip", "_value"])

list.name: site
list.label: Site
list.description: Which tzsp-monitor instance these panels read. Remote sites are the REMOTE_SITE_* lines in properties.yml of the instance serving this Grafana; each is a datasource pointed at that site's own InfluxDB, so nothing is copied between sites. Controls never follow this box: rule suppression and reverse DNS only ever act on the local site, and are inert while another site is selected.

list.name: health_talkers
list.label: Busiest hosts (internal)
list.description: Hidden helper: the 8 busiest source IPs, fed to the reverse-DNS resolver.
list.query:
from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 8)
  |> keep(columns: ["src_ip"])
  |> rename(columns: {src_ip: "_value"})
